items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Follow up to #53636

This Pull Request has been created to fix regclass cast to be schema-qualified.

Detail

The UPDATE pg_constraint SET convalidated=false inside check_all_foreign_keys_valid! matches by conrelid::regclass = '%3$I'::regclass, but 'orders'::regclass resolves using search_path — so when two schemas each contain a table named orders, both their FK constraints get reset to NOT VALID, but only the one being processed gets re-validated. The other schema's FK is permanently left NOT VALID.

When two schemas each contain a table with the same name and a FK constraint with the same name, the unqualified conrelid::regclass cast in the UPDATE resolved via search_path and could reset convalidated=false on the wrong schema's constraint, leaving it permanently NOT VALID. After check_all_foreign_keys_valid! both must be convalidated = true. Before the fix, the search_path-ambiguous UPDATE reset convalidated=false on whichever schema came second in the loop, leaving it permanently invalid.

One token changes in the FORMAT string: replace the bare '%3$I'::regclass cast with a schema-qualified '%2$I.%3$I'::regclass cast. We have added a test case also.

Additional information

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Fixes #57401

When running tests in parallel with processes (parallelize / PARALLEL_WORKERS), the parent process starts a DRb service in Parallelization#initialize via DRb.start_service. However, #shutdown only shut down the queue server and waited for workers; it never called DRb.stop_service.

As a result, the parent kept a DRb accept-loop thread alive after workers exited. In some environments, this prevented the test process from exiting, for example CI timing out after printing 0 failures. Worker processes already call DRb.stop_service after fork, so only the parent was missing cleanup.

Detail

  • Call DRb.stop_service at the end of ActiveSupport::Testing::Parallelization#shutdown, after all worker processes have been reaped with Process.waitpid
  • Add a regression test that asserts no DRb accept threads remain after shutdown

Additional information

I verified the following locally:

  • With the fix: bin/test test/parallelization_test.rb -i "/shutdown stops the DRb/" passes
  • Without DRb.stop_service, the same test fails with a leaked DRb accept thread, verified locally

items.content_html:
when a base-class association is preloaded alongside a subclass association.

Fixes #57387

Motivation / Background

When preloading a base-class has_many :through association (e.g. :categories)
alongside an STI subclass has_many :through association (e.g. :special_categories)
on the same through table, the subclass association's target would be incorrectly
populated with records of sibling STI types.

Detail

ThroughAssociation#records_by_owner builds its result by flat-mapping
source_records_by_owner over the through records. Because source_records_by_owner
is seeded from the through join model's belongs_to :source reflection — which points
to the base class — the SQL query it issues has no STI WHERE type = ? filter.
When the base-class association has already been preloaded (and thus the through
records are already cached), all source records of all STI sibling types end up in
source_records_by_owner, and the subclass association gets all of them.

The fix filters records by reflection.klass after the flat-map when the
association targets an STI subclass (reflection.klass != reflection.klass.base_class).
reflection.klass is SpecialCategory (from class_name: "SpecialCategory"), so
is_a?(reflection.klass) correctly rejects sibling types without affecting
non-STI associations.

Additional information

The bug is reproducible with any preload order that includes both a base-class
through association and an STI subclass through association sharing the same
join model. Standalone loads and single-association preloads are unaffected because
they hit the correct filtered SQL path directly.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

After parallelized test runs, the parent process leaks the Active Record Pool Reaper thread, holding open connection pools and file descriptors indefinitely. In long-lived CI processes running many suites sequentially this accumulates threads and open DB connections.

Fixes #57402

Detail

Three layered bugs caused the leak:

  1. Parallelization#shutdown never called run_cleanup_hooks, so no parent-side cleanup ran at all.
  2. AR never registered a run_cleanup_hook to discard its pools.
  3. clear_all_connections! calls disconnect! not discard!, so even if a hook had been registered the reaper thread would not have been stopped.

This PR fixes all three: Parallelization#shutdown now calls run_cleanup_hooks after workers finish; Active Record registers a cleanup hook that calls discard! on all connection pools; and ConnectionPool#discard! now calls Reaper.discard_pool, which removes the pool from the reaper's registry and immediately kills and joins the reaper thread if no pools remain at that frequency.

Additional information

Reproduction script:

require "bundler/inline"
gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"
  gem "rails", github: "rails/rails", branch: "main"
  gem "sqlite3"
end
require "active_support"
require "active_support/testing/parallelization"
require "active_record"
require "active_record/test_databases"
require "minitest/autorun"

ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(
  adapter: "sqlite3",
  database: ":memory:",
  reaping_frequency: 5
)
ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.with_connection { |c| c.execute("SELECT 1") }
sleep 0.1

class ARPoolReaperLeakTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_ar_pool_reaper_is_cleaned_up_after_parallelization_shutdown
    assert Thread.list.find { |t| t.name == "Active Record Pool Reaper" }

    parallelization = ActiveSupport::Testing::Parallelization.new(1)
    parallelization.start
    parallelization.shutdown

    assert_empty Thread.list.select { |t| t.alive? && t.name == "Active Record Pool Reaper" }
  end
end

items.content_html:
Summary

This adds internal predicate-builder hooks that let Active Record attribute types customize how attributes and query values are represented in hash where predicates.

Types can define:

  • query_attribute(attribute) to transform the left-hand side of predicates
  • query_value(attribute, value, predicate_builder:) to transform bound values while preserving prepared binds

The predicate builder uses these hooks for basic equality predicates, array predicates, and ranges.

Why this is needed

Some database-backed types need a different SQL representation for reads than for writes.

One case is a text column that stores the original user-provided value, but should compare using a normalized expression such as:

lower(custom_immutable_unaccent(name)) = lower(custom_immutable_unaccent(?))

The value cannot be normalized in cast or serialize, because that would change the stored value. It needs to be normalized only when building predicates.

Another case is a MySQL UUID type stored in binary(16), where callers should be able to pass readable UUID strings while the predicate renders the value as:

id = UUID_TO_BIN(?)

That is intentionally asymmetric: the column is already binary, but the query value needs a SQL conversion function.

Alternatives without this

Today these cases require one of a few awkward options:

  • Normalize in the attribute type with cast or serialize, which changes storage semantics and cannot preserve the original value.
  • Define custom scopes for every affected predicate, which loses the ergonomics of where(name: value), where(name: values), and range predicates.
  • Register custom PredicateBuilder handlers for wrapper value objects, which requires callers to wrap every query value and does not work naturally with plain hash where values.
  • Monkey-patch Arel visitors to detect specific bind attributes and wrap SQL there. That is adapter-global, private API, and hard to make correct for IN, BETWEEN, nil predicates, and write queries.
  • Use raw SQL fragments, which gives up type casting, bind handling, and composability.

Keeping the behavior on the Active Record type lets the model opt in once with attribute, while leaving storage behavior in cast / serialize and predicate behavior in these query-specific hooks.

Verification

  • ruby -c on changed Ruby files
  • Focused bin/test could not run in this checkout because Bundler reports missing local gems: msgpack, nokogiri, rails-html-sanitizer, and loofah.
items.title: Add query predicate hooks for Active Record types

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Follow up to #46486

This Pull Request has been created to reconstruct new change objects for became, not mutate the shared ones.

Detail

@attachment_changes is a plain hash of change objects. super (ActiveRecord's becomes) does not deep-copy them — both the original record and became hold references to the exact same CreateOne/CreateMany objects. When instance_variable_set(:@record, became) runs, it writes through to those shared objects, so original_record.attachment_changes["avatar"].record now points to became instead of to the original. Saving the original after the cast silently uploads the file to the wrong record or no-ops entirely. The fix should deep-dup the hash and create new change objects, not mutate shared ones.

With this PR transform_values on a new hash leaves the original hash and its objects completely untouched. case change on the concrete class - Each change class has a different constructor signature, so we can rebuild them cleanly; pattern-matching is safer than duck-typing here. (@attachment_changes || {}) guards against the ivar being nil before lazy init, matching initialize_dup's pattern. Original @attachment_changes is never written to. The original record can still be saved independently after becomes. We have added relevant test cases in the PR.

Additional information

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

When running rails generate migration SomeMigration without an explicit --database option, the generator always writes to db/migrate path, even if the primary database is configured with a custom migrations_paths (e.g. db/migrate_primary).

Detail

The bug lived in configured_migrate_path, which returned early when no --database option was given:

def configured_migrate_path
  return unless database = options[:database]
  # ...
end

This PR removes the early return, so when --database is not given, the generator now looks up the primary configuration and uses its migrations_paths instead of falling back to db/migrate.

A regression test in migration_generator_test.rb covers a multi-DB setup and asserts the migration lands in the primary's migrations_paths rather than db/migrate.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

There are a couple of examples in the Guides of how to use association callbacks (before_add etc). In one example, the callback loads an association (books) and performs validation based on the count of books. Personally, I avoid calling associations in callbacks because it can lead to N+1s and makes the code difficult to test. Plus, the validation in that kind of callback doesn't cover the scenario where one calls Book.create(author: author) directly.

I understand that many like to call associations in callbacks, so you'll find arguments on both sides. In any case, I think the example should be more agnostic and simpler to keep the focus on the callback mechanics and less on side-effects and usages. Readers may decide how best to use use the callback according to their preferences.

There was also an example with two callbacks, but I couldn't understand the goal of the second callback. It didn't appear to change any state and had a return value with no clear purpose.

Detail

This Pull Request simplifies the first association callback example to use simple logging. The second example is shortened. I think it conveys the idea clearly enough. The PR also moves a couple of sentences to organize the flow of the text a bit. I kept the warning about the effects of throw :abort in there as reminder for people who might want to do validation in these.

Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created to improve the Rails Internationalization docs.

Detail

A big change is that I've reordered the guide to start off with beginner friendly content, then move into managing locales in requests (as its own section for easier navigation), then API features and finally an advaced section.

Other parts tackled from here:

  • Remove the Contributing section which references a inactive forum.
  • Remove the authors section, as we don't mention the authors in other guides.
  • Unlike other guides the introduction does a quick summation of steps to take to implement I18n. The whole introduction should probably be rewritten with a "After reading this guide, you will know..."
  • "This means, that in the :en locale, the key hello will map to the Hello world string. " This could probably be replaced with a code example:
    I18n.t('hello')
    => "Hello world"
  • Code examples would also improve the mentioned ActiveModel validation messages.
  • "Managing the Locale across Requests" should probably be a top section.
  • - The first example of setting the locale through a param is missing a header. Something like: "Setting the Locale from a request parameter"
  • - In the "Passing Variables to Translations" section the product_price switches from $ to € which is probably not typical. Maybe a better example would be using "dutch" and "spanish" where dutch uses "€ 100" and spanish "100 €".
  • - The note about number_to_currency should probably be a NOTE instead.
  • - The line "(Future Rails versions may well bring this automagic localization to assets in public, etc.)" can probably be removed, as I don't think this has been implemented or is planned.
  • [ ]
  • - The returned values for the examples in "Basic Lookup, Scopes, and Nested Keys" would make things clearer.
  • - The resulting HTML for "app/views/home/index.html.erb " in "Using Safe HTML Translations" is missing. This would help in seeing what gets escaped and what doesn't.
  • - The example usage in "Translations for Active Record Models" like User.model_name.human are probably clearer in a code block.
  • - The methods mentioned in "Overview of Other Built-In Methods that Provide I18n Support" would be clearer with code examples.
  • - The "Custom Translations" examples are more clear if we also show the output:
  • I18n.t "date.formats.short" # => "%b %d"
  • [ ]
  • - The "Using Different Backends" section shows an example how to add a different backend, but doesn't go into detail on how to use that backend.
  • - The "Using Different Exception Handlers" also mentions how to configure Rails to handle MissingTranslationData exceptions. That section should probably be renamed "Handling Missing Translations" or "Handling I18n Exceptions". This section could probably use an example as well:
  • > I18n.t('missing')
  • Translation missing: en.missing (I18n::MissingTranslationData)
  • and maybe examples can be added for the other exceptions as well?
  • - The "Translating Model Content" section should not link to 3rd party gems. This section should probably just be a note in the introduction instead.
  • [ ]

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because Rails is missing a way to insert arbitrary load hooks for specific autoloadable classes. Zeitwerk has support for this with on_load("MyClassName"), but Rails doesn't provide a public-api-friendly way of accessing the Zeitwerk loader in Rails (the only way is Rails.autoloaders.main, which is private API). Even if you were to use this API, the semantics here are slightly different to ActiveSupport.on_load.

Detail

This Pull Request adds ActiveSupport.on_module_load to fill this gap. Instead of using to_prepare to eagerly load a class:

Rails.configuration.to_prepare do
  MyClassName.config = true
end

We can now instead do something like this:

ActiveSupport.on_module_load(:MyClassName) do
  self.config = true
end

Additional information

More information here: #57224

Summary

Also support dynamic store: option in rate_limit like we already do for some of the other params.

Motivation / Background

The rate_limit API supports method names and callables for some of the parameters.
Extending this to :store allows applications to resolve the cache store at runtime (per-request, per-tenant, gradual cache migrations, etc.) without boilerplate conditionals in controllers. Static usages untouched.

Detail

Changes ActionController::RateLimiting so that store: accepts:

  • Static values (unchanged behavior), e.g. store: RedisCacheStore.new(...).
  • Instance method names (symbols), evaluated in the controller context via send (like we already do for to and within).
  • Callables (lambdas/procs), evaluated in the controller context via instance_exec following the existing pattern.

Resolution logic:

  • If value is a Symbol → send(value)
  • Else if it responds to call → instance_exec(&value)
  • Else → use as-is

Additional information

  • Aligns with earlier changes to allow method names for :to, :within, :by, and :with.
  • Negligible overhead (a couple of conditional checks) on the rate-limited path.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

When using multiple databases you traditionally can't join across databases but SQLite has the unique ability to include different SQLite databases in the connection and treat them one big database.

Take this setup for example:

class ApplicationRecord < ActiveRecord::Base
  self.abstract_class = true
end

class Course < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :entrants
end

class OtherRecord < ActiveRecord::Base
  self.abstract_class = true

  connects_to database: { writing: :other }
end

class Entrant < OtherRecord
  belongs_to :course
end
default: &default
  adapter: sqlite3

development:
  primary:
    <<: *default
    database: storage/dev.sqlite3
  other:
    <<: *default
    migrations_paths: db/other_migrate
    database: storage/other_dev.sqlite3

Prior to this patch if you were to execute Entrant.joins(:course).where(courses: { name: "Ruby Development" }), a StatementInvalid error will be raised because Entrant and Course live in different databases. But if you execute ATTACH DATABASE 'storage/other_dev.sqlite3' as other, you bring entrants into scope and can join over to it. This patch prepends the database name to those external database table calls to avoid conflicts.

Given that we know where these models live, database wise, and SQLite offers us the an avenue to join across databases, we should automatically include those databases into scope and extract that away from the developer when executing a query.

Since SQLite can be write constrained, if you have a particularly write heavy table, this would allow you to move the table to it's own database and free up the primary database for more writes while still allowing you to treat it as if it was in the primary database.

Additional information

sqlite docs on attach
